method: eval_transcription.dash_turn_points (human two-speaker '- A / - B' single cues)
as ground truth, time-matched at tol=0.6s
ground_truth_caveat: Only 12 turn points exist in this ground truth for the whole
episode (10025 words) -- it only captures a speaker change that
happens to be rendered as ONE two-line dash cue in the human
subtitle, not every real speaker change (most show up as ordinary
consecutive cues, invisible to this measurement). Recall is a weak
signal (n=12); precision against this sparse a positive set is not
trustworthy at all and should not be read as a real false-positive rate.

runs.label: heuristic (first cut: PAUSE_THRESHOLD=0.5s, SHORT_REPLY_WORDS=4, no minimum
gap required for the question/short-reply signals)
voice (WeSpeaker ResNet34 ONNX, CPU, numpy fbank; similarity_threshold=0.6)
heuristic (retuned: PAUSE_THRESHOLD=0.6s, SHORT_REPLY_WORDS=2,
MIN_TURN_GAP=0.15s required for the question/short-reply signals)

decision: Both detectors over-trigger far past what's usable in production (>10% of
words would become a speaker-turn boundary -- for context, a real
multi-character scene has nowhere near that turn density), and the available
ground truth (12 points) cannot validate precision at all. Heuristic is the
clearly better of the two on the numbers that ARE meaningful (recall,
runtime: instant vs 110s/episode on CPU) if one had to be picked, but neither
clears the bar to ship as a default. Code, tests, and the env-var toggle are
shipped so this can be revisited with better ground truth (e.g. a small
hand-annotated clip) without redoing the implementation.
